name: Lowend
sources: style-research-extended vol.3 — finding 7: `lowend` (Milwaukee — sourced as "8th-note handclaps + snares on 1 and 3", and it is the two-tier kit that `jerk` destabilises); `jerk` claims Certified Trapper and J.P. as a declared exception precisely because no `lowend` model exists to hold them

style-research-extended vol.3 jerk — "Lowend is documented as using 'synthesized eighth-note handclaps in steady, metronome-like rhythm' with 'snares on beats 1 and 3' and characterised as 'uptempo, metronome-like clapping rhythms, heavy bass, and snares', 'danceable and minimalistic'"
style-research-extended vol.3 jerk — "Note the inverted convention: snares on 1 and 3, claps on the 8ths — not the usual backbeat-on-2&4 arrangement"

style-research-extended vol.3 jerk — the tempo spine: "Lowend's own tempo spine reads 170–186 (`Opp Bxtch` 181, `Slipped Up` 186, `Slime` 184, `Palm Angels` 178, `Certified Trapper Meter`/`TC`/`Trapper Of The Year` 178, `Morty` 177, `Each Smack` 172) with the halved twin at 92–99"
style-research-extended vol.3 jerk — "Lowend contributes the movement: its bass is 'rumbling, heavy' and continuous rather than punctual"
notes: Milwaukee's own lane, and the archetype `jerk` was documented as *borrowing from* while having nowhere to send it. ⛔⛔ **THE ENGINE COULD NOT SPELL THIS GENRE UNTIL 2026-08-15, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE.** The research states the cell as an inversion — *"snares on 1 and 3, claps on the 8ths — not the usual backbeat-on-2&4 arrangement"* — and `SnarePlacement::parse` read exactly two names, `halftime_3` and `backbeat_24`. A snare on 1 and 3 is neither. `drums.rs` now carries a third, `downbeat_1_3`, and this is the model it was added for; without it the lane could only have been faked with a backbeat, which is the one thing the research says it is not. ⛔ **The two-tier kit is the second half, and it is what `jerk` destabilises.** *"A rigid, perfectly-quantised 8th-note clap stream running underneath a violently off-grid snare cluster tier. Build it as two separate instruments — the clap is a metronome, the snare is the improviser."* Here the metronome wins: `quantizeStrength` is 0.95 and the jitter is near zero, because *this* lane is the rigid one — `jerk` is the model that takes the same DNA and randomises the snare, and its own gate (`jerk_is_the_one_genre_that_asks_to_be_loosened`) exists to keep it the loosest thing on the roster. ⚠ **The clap stream is authored as the hat lane, and the reason is structural.** `Lane::Clap` is not in `PERC_LANES` — the clap in this engine is a *layer on the snare*, placed by `layerClapOffsetMs` — so an independent eighth-note clap stream has no lane of its own. What is authored is the **grammar**: `hihat.base` is `"8th"`, `continuous`, at a flat velocity band and with rolls all but switched off, which is a metronome. Which sample voices it is a kit decision, the same answer `chicago-bounce` gives for its ride. ⚠ **The bass is continuous rather than punctual**, which is the sourced word: *"rumbling, heavy"*, and the movement Milwaukee contributes to jerk is *"a walking 808, 4 to 8 onsets per bar stepping through the scale"*. The 808 is the bass here (`role: "bassline"`) and it is locked to a busy kick, because this engine's 808 plays a subset of the kick's onsets and nothing else — so the walk has to be authored as kick density, which is what `densityPerBar: [4, 7]` with `lockTo808: 1` is doing. ⚠ **Tempo: the fast spine, not the halved twin.** 170–186 centred on 178, from eight catalogue readings. The halved 92–99 reading is the same records notated at half speed and is deliberately not a second mode — unlike `michigan-offgrid`, where two *different* bodies of work sit in the two bands. ⚠ **INFERRED, hence `medium`.** Sourced: the tempo spine and its eight readings, the snare on 1 and 3, the eighth-note clap stream, the metronomic quantisation, the heavy continuous bass and the "danceable and minimalistic" framing. Inferred: every velocity tier, every register, the key and scale lists, the whole harmony block (the research names none for this lane, which is consistent with "minimalistic"), and the mode names. ⚠ **Nothing was moved onto this model.** `jerk` still carries Certified Trapper and J.P. as its declared exception; moving them is a roster change with its own gates.
